beats.notes: frost drop falls on grid, push-in
match-cut: drop becomes pump rotor, spins
rotor opens into chamber, flame sketch draws on
pull-back: full rocket stack outline
upper stage glows amber, rest dim, label FINAL PUSH
empty box where the engine should be, "?" pulses once
stamp-less text: "NOT PHYSICS. TRANSFER."

lines: WHEN THE ONE ENGINE YOU NEED
IS THE ONE YOU CANNOT GET?

beats.notes: question draws on: SO WHAT DO YOU DO WHEN THE ONE ENGINE YOU NEED IS THE ONE YOU CANNOT GET?
tick on a bare timeline: EARLY 1990s
gate drawn across a pipeline (concept: restrictions on access), label RESTRICTED ACCESS
engine silhouette behind the gate, others' engines faint ghosts (no country marks)
two engineers at a bench look at a drawing, point
"A refusal does not create an engine" draws on as a stroke title
puzzle: pieces assemble one by one on the bench (pump, valve, seal, chamber, nozzle)
counter ticks "ONE PIECE AT A TIME" (no number)
pieces slide into the engine
hold: three words, STUBBORN. TESTED. REPEATED.
cook lights gas stove, flame blue-amber
fuel + oxygen arrows merge at flame, label FUEL + OXYGEN = HEAT
rocket tank cutaway: carries its own oxygen, label OWN OXYGEN
tank frosts, thermometer glyph dives, label VERY COLD (no number unless sourced)
pipe-network shrinks slightly (contraction arrows), label PLUMBING UNFORGIVING
hold on tank + pipes together
cyclist pumps tyre, one push per beat
air arrow through a narrow passage
turbopump appears in cutaway, impeller spins
flow arrows: fuel in, pressure up, out to chamber, gauge rises
two lines: TINY HAND PUMP vs TURBOPUMP, scale-ghost
fail state: pump slows, gauge falls, chamber flame fades
label WITHOUT FLOW, NO ENGINE
pressure cooker, steam rattles
chamber section appears (clipping plane sweeps)
gas speeds through throat, particles accelerate (seeded)
nozzle bell draws on, exhaust goes backward, rocket nudges forward
heat/cold wall: amber inside, cyan cooling passages outside (concept)
callouts pop one at a time: MATERIALS · SEALS · COOLING · VALVES
all four light up together, label EVERYTHING COOPERATES
outline of an engine, empty; "COPY THE OUTLINE"
ghost layers of invisible behaviour fill inside (flow, heat, vibration) as dashed lines
test loop draws: TEST - FAIL - CHANGE - TEST, arrow circulates twice
hold
timeline strip: EARLY GSLV FLIGHTS - CRYOGENIC STAGES SUPPLIED FROM ABROAD
tick JAN 2014 - FIRST INDIGENOUS CRYOGENIC STAGE FLIES (ISRO)
rocket stack, upper stage highlighted, label CE20 ON LVM3
counter ticks to 8 SUCCESSIVE LVM3 MISSIONS (ISRO), Chandrayaan-3 tag
22 TONNES OF THRUST card on a dimension chain, source chip "ISRO, 6 JUL 2026"
engine in test-stand sketch, flame (concept)
text: NOT A SINGLE TEST. A CAPABILITY THAT REPEATS.
pull-back: 8 small rocket marks line up
FICTIONAL SCENARIO stamp across the frame for the whole passage
rocket ready on pad, assembled
pump gauge a notch low
chamber starved: flame thin and flickering (no flicker artefact; designed pulse)
mission arc fades short of orbit
text: RELIABILITY IN EVERY HIDDEN PART
heading THE STORY IS NOT FINISHED
four empty boxes draw one by one: HIGHER PERFORMANCE · MORE CAPABLE STAGES · MANUFACTURING CONSISTENCY · FUTURE PROPULSION
two hands-joined glyph labelled INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION STILL VALUABLE
the opening question re-appears: CAN AN UNAVAILABLE ENGINE STOP A PROGRAMME?
answer draws as a stroke over it: YEARS OF TESTING
text: CAPABLE ONLY WHEN IT WORKS
frozen drop returns, rotor, chamber (reverse of P01)
camera pulls back to the full rocket rising, line-drawn
final line holds: A CLOSED DOOR IS NOT A FINISHED STORY.
